name: Residenztheater (Bayerisches Staatsschauspiel)
overview: The Bavarian State Theatre for spoken drama plays in three venues near the Munich Residenz: the Residenztheater on Max-Joseph-Platz with 881 seats, the Cuvilliéstheater with 437 seats and the Marstall with about 146 seats (theatre website).
It grew out of the princely court and national theatre of the 18th century; the royal court theatre became the Staatstheater after the revolution of 1918 (theatre website; German Wikipedia).
It is one of four Bavarian State Theatres in Munich, with the State Opera, the Theatre Academy August Everding at the Prinzregententheater and the Gärtnerplatztheater (theatre website).
funding_verdict: Residenztheater: public: the Free State of Bavaria, with a friends' association and foundations on single projects

name: Museum Abteiberg
overview: Municipal museum of contemporary art in the historic centre of Mönchengladbach, built into the face of a hillside next to the cathedral and a baroque abbey (hollein.com).
Called the Städtisches Museum Abteiberg. The city of Mönchengladbach was the client, planning ran 1972 to 1973 and the building was completed in 1982 (hollein.com).

Designed by the Austrian architect Hans Hollein. The building is a walk-on structure whose surface is open to the public and used for open-air sculpture, and the interior is a sequence of white spaces arranged as a three-dimensional matrix rather than a linear route (hollein.com).
funding_verdict: Museum Abteiberg: mainly public: the city of Mönchengladbach

name: Hong Kong Arts Festival
overview: The Hong Kong Arts Festival is a non-profit organisation launched in 1973 (festival website).
The pages read did not name a building or a founder.
What is there: the festival presents an annual programme; the 55th Festival and the 2027 No Limits programme fall in the 2026/27 budget (festival website).
funding_verdict: Hong Kong Arts Festival: mainly private: sponsorship and donations target about 44 percent, government baseline about 11 percent

name: Mehrangarh Museum Trust
overview: A museum in Mehrangarh Fort, Jodhpur, with its own visitor, conservation and research programmes (Trust website).
The Trust was founded in 1972 by H.H. Maharaja Gaj Singhji, the 36th Custodian of Marwar-Jodhpur, and registered with the Government of Rajasthan in 1974 (Trust website).

What is there: fine and applied arts from the Mughal period and the Rathore rulers, in the categories paintings, textiles, arms and armour, decorative arts and publications, with examples from the 17th to 19th centuries (Trust website).
funding_verdict: Mehrangarh Museum Trust: funding not stated on the pages read

name: Anu Museum of the Jewish People
aliases: Anu - Museum of the Jewish People
overview: The museum of the Jewish people, on Tel Aviv University's campus, formerly Beit Hatfutsot (AP via KOMO, 10 March 2021).
Reopened in March 2021 after more than a decade of renovation; exhibition space tripled to 72,000 square feet (AP via KOMO, 10 March 2021).

What is there: objects including a jawza instrument from the Al-Kuwaity brothers, a Ruth Bader Ginsburg collar, a pre-Inquisition Book of Esther scroll and a first-century carved stone from a Galilee synagogue (AP via KOMO, 10 March 2021). No total count was given.
funding_verdict: Anu Museum of the Jewish People: mixed, large private and US gifts plus an Israeli government share.

name: Teatro Carlo Felice
aliases: Fondazione Teatro Carlo Felice di Genova
overview: Opera and ballet foundation of Genoa, a private-law foundation whose statute was approved by decree on 29 December 2014 and amended on 20 December 2016 (Ministry of Culture page).
Its board for 22 April 2025 to 22 April 2030 is chaired by the mayor, Silvia Salis (Ministry of Culture page).
What is there: lyric and ballet activity (Ministry of Culture page). The pages read did not describe its holdings or archive.
funding_verdict: Teatro Carlo Felice: mainly public: State fund plus Comune and Region, with Iren

name: Castello Sforzesco
aliases: Civiche Raccolte d'Arte del Castello Sforzesco
overview: The Castello Sforzesco in Milan houses the city's Civic Collections, among them the Collections of Ancient Art within the Museums Area directed by Francesca Tasso (Finestre sull'Arte, 24 February 2025).

What is there: Mantegna's Pala Trivulzio entered the Civic Collections in 1935, when the City of Milan acquired the Trivulzio Collection, which included a library, late antique ivories, paintings and a tapestry cycle of the Months; the Sala delle Asse holds wall decorations attributed to Leonardo da Vinci (Finestre sull'Arte, 24 February 2025; 4 August 2024).
funding_verdict: Castello Sforzesco: municipal, with Fondazione Cariplo and private donors paying for restorations.

name: Museo Nazionale della Scienza e della Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci
aliases: Museo della Scienza e della Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci
Fondazione Museo nazionale della scienza e della tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci
overview: The Museo Nazionale della Scienza e della Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci is a museum in Milan, inaugurated on 15 February 1953 and run since 1 January 2000 as a private-law foundation (Corte dei conti report on 2024).

Its aim is the study and communication of the work of Leonardo da Vinci and of science and technology, through research, conservation and updating of its collections, archives and library (Corte dei conti report on 2024).

What is there: over 170 historic models, works of art, old volumes and installations about Leonardo, and a heritage of 15,000 technical-scientific and artistic objects, over 50,000 square metres, 15 exhibition sections and 13 interactive laboratories (Corte dei conti report on 2024).
funding_verdict: Museo Nazionale della Scienza e della Tecnologia: public money from three ministries and local bodies, plus a growing share from private fundraising.

name: Piccolo Teatro di Milano
aliases: Piccolo Teatro di Milano - Teatro d'Europa
overview: A theatre of Milan with four venues: Teatro Strehler at Largo Greppi 1, Teatro Grassi at Via Rovello 2, Teatro Studio Melato at Via Rivoli 6 and the Chiostro Nina Vinchi (theatre website).
The site logo reads 1947 to 2027; legal address is Via Rovello 2 (theatre website).
What is there: a repertory and touring theatre company with a theatre school and associate artists; Claudio Longhi is artistic director and Lanfranco Li Cauli CEO (theatre website).
funding_verdict: Piccolo Teatro di Milano: public, State plus city and region founders, with corporate patrons.

name: Madre · museo d'arte contemporanea Donnaregina
overview: Contemporary art museum at Via Luigi Settembrini 79, in Naples' historic centre (museum website; arte.it).
Founded by the Campania Region. The Fondazione Donnaregina per le arti contemporanee runs it (arte.it).
Named for the Palazzo Donnaregina, which takes its name from the 13th-century monastery of Santa Maria Donnaregina (arte.it).
funding_verdict: Madre: mainly public: the Campania Region

press_items.title: Maria Adelaide Marchesoni, "Cercasi nuovo direttore per il Madre, troppo dipendente dai contributi pubblici" (2022)
Giovanna Procaccini, "Fondazione Donnaregina e Madre. Da otto a uno" (2012), interview with Pierpaolo Forte

name: Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Napoli
overview: National archaeological museum at Piazza Museo 18/19, Naples, known as the MANN (museum website).

It grew from Charles of Bourbon's plan, after he took the throne of Naples in 1734, to excavate the Vesuvian towns and bring part of his Farnese inheritance to Naples; it opened officially as the Real Museo Borbonico in 1816 and was renamed National Museum after Italian unification in 1860 (museum website).

Building: a late 16th-century royal cavalry barracks that housed the University of Naples from 1616 to 1777, then enlarged by the architects Fuga and Schiantarelli; the paintings left for Capodimonte in 1957, leaving a purely archaeological museum (museum website).
funding_verdict: Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Napoli: public: the Italian Ministry of Culture

press_items.title: editorial staff, "Napoli, il mosaico di Alessandro va in mostra in Giappone? Il MANN: 'nessun accordo'" (2021)

name: Castello di Rivoli Museo d Arte Contemporanea
overview: Contemporary art museum in a former residence of the House of Savoy at Rivoli, near Turin. It opened as a museum in 1984 and is described by Wikipedia as the first contemporary art museum in Italy.

Castle history: first mentioned in 1159, used as barracks from 1863, heavily damaged in the Second World War and restored from 1979. Andrea Bruno was the architect of the first post-war renovation (Wikipedia). It is one of 14 Savoy residences on the UNESCO World Heritage list since 1997.

Directors: Rudi Fuchs and Johannes Gachnang (1984 to 1991), Ida Giannelli (1991 to 2008), Andrea Bellini and Beatrice Merz (2010 to 2014), Carolyn Christov-Bakargiev (2015 to 2024) and Francesco Manacorda from 2024 (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Castello di Rivoli: mainly public money plus two private foundations: Regione Piemonte, City of Turin, Town of Rivoli, Fondazione CRT and Compagnia di San Paolo

name: Museo Nazionale del Cinema
overview: The Museo Nazionale del Cinema is a film museum housed in the Mole Antonelliana in Turin, run by a foundation (museum website; 2024 management report).

The founding members are Regione Piemonte, Città di Torino, Fondazione Compagnia di San Paolo, Fondazione CRT, GTT and the Associazione Museo Nazionale del Cinema; the Ministry of Culture contributes (museum website).

What is there: the site lists Collections, the Mario Gromo library and mediatheque, Historical Archives, Film Archives and a Film Restoration Laboratory; the museum also runs the Cinema Massimo, the Torino Film Festival, CinemAmbiente, Lovers Film Festival and TorinoFilmLab. The pages read gave no object counts (museum website).
funding_verdict: Museo Nazionale del Cinema: public bodies and bank foundations pay most of it, with the Ministry the largest single funder in 2024.

name: Reggia di Venaria
overview: The Reggia di Venaria is a baroque royal palace of 80,000 square metres with 60 hectares of gardens at Venaria Reale near Turin, next to the 3,000 hectare La Mandria park, declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997 (Venaria press kit 2007 to 2025).
It opened to the public on 12 October 2007 after 8 years of restoration following two centuries of neglect (Venaria press kit 2007 to 2025).

The consortium was set up by public deed on 30 June 2008 among the Ministry of Culture, Regione Piemonte, the Città di Venaria Reale, the Compagnia di San Paolo and its art foundation, now Fondazione 1563 per l'arte e la cultura (Regione Piemonte resolution, 14 April 2025).
funding_verdict: Reggia di Venaria: mainly public and foundation money through a consortium, with 38% of the budget earned.

name: Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum
overview: Public art museum at 8-36 Ueno Park, Taito-ku, Tokyo, seven minutes' walk from the Park Gate of JR Ueno station (museum website).

It opened on 1 May 1926 as the Tokyo Prefectural Art Museum, Japan's first public art museum, after the coal industrialist Sato Keitaro (1868 to 1940), known as the "god of coal" (石炭の神様, own translation), moved by a 1922 newspaper article calling for a permanent museum, gave 1 million yen to build it (museum website, centenary exhibition page).

Buildings: the first, with columns and a grand staircase, was by Okada Shin'ichiro; Maekawa Kunio designed the 1975 replacement, with the main floor below ground and several blocks around a central plaza (museum website).
funding_verdict: Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum: public: the Tokyo Metropolitan Government, with newspaper and corporate partners for big shows

name: The Jordan Museum
overview: National museum of Jordan's archaeology and history in Amman's Ras Al Ain area, in a building of about 10,000 square metres (The Jordan Times, 12 February 2017; The National, 13 March 2014).

Director general Ihab Amarin said a Jordan Museum had been a national dream since the 1960s; its first phase, from the Palaeolithic to the end of the Classical period, opened in 2013 (The Jordan Times, 2017). The National reported a soft opening in January 2013, with Sharifa Nofa Bint Nasser as director.

A royal decree of 2002 established a national museum; Queen Rania, chair of the board of trustees, laid its cornerstone at Ras El Ein on 2 October 2005, after building work on the three-storey museum had begun that year (Jordan News, 13 April 2021; Office of Queen Rania, 3 October 2005). The chief architect was the late Jafar Tukan (Jordan News).
funding_verdict: The Jordan Museum: public: the Jordanian state, with a building paid for in part by a Japanese yen loan

name: Fondation H
overview: Contemporary art foundation in the centre of Antananarivo, at the foot of the Queen's Palace and the Prime Minister's palace (The Art Newspaper France, Anaël Pigeat, 23 June 2023).
Founded in 2017 by the entrepreneur and patron Hassanein Hiridjee, who is its president. Madagascar has recognised it as a public-utility foundation since 2018 (the foundation's website).
Hiridjee began the collection in 2010. Its about 200 works all belong to the foundation (The Art Newspaper France, 2023).
funding_verdict: Fondation H: private: founded and presided over by Axian chief executive Hassanein Hiridjee, with free entry

name: Museo Nacional de Arte
overview: Mexico's national art museum at Tacuba 8 in the historic centre of Mexico City, in the former headquarters of the Secretaría de Comunicaciones y Obras Públicas, built from 1904 to 1911 under the Italian architect Silvio Contri (museum website).
It opened in 1982 as the Museo Nacional de Arte (museum website).

The collection is about 10,000 pieces. Named funds: Félix Parra, 444 items bought by INBAL in 2008 and in the museum's custody since 2010; Luis G. Serrano, 250 artworks given in 2008; María Asúnsolo, 49 items given in 1987, 1988 and 1993, with portraits of her by Siqueiros, Soriano, Rivera, Cantú and Di Cavalcanti; Ricardo Pérez Escamilla, acquired in 2010, with 1,505 graphic works, chiefly 19th-century lithographs; and Elsa Rogo, 377 artworks given in 2011 by James Oles (museum website).
funding_verdict: Museo Nacional de Arte: public, INBAL, with a private Patronato and sponsors

name: Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech
overview: Museum devoted to the work of fashion designer Yves Saint Laurent, on Rue Yves Saint Laurent near the Jardin Majorelle in Marrakech (Wikipedia; Fondation Jardin Majorelle press release, 15 November 2022).
Inaugurated in October 2017 and opened to the public on 19 October 2017 (Wikipedia).

Pierre Bergé said it was "natural to build a museum dedicated to the work of Yves Saint Laurent in Morocco" (Wikipedia). It shows the collection of the Pierre Bergé - Yves Saint Laurent Foundation. A second museum for the collection stands at the former fashion house headquarters in Paris (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech: privately funded: Pierre Bergé's sale of Moroccan art, run by the Fondation Jardin Majorelle

name: Anne Frank House
overview: The canal house at Prinsengracht 263 to 267 in Amsterdam with the Secret Annex where Anne Frank and seven others hid, entered at Westermarkt 20; an organisation of about 250 employees runs the museum, manages the collection, makes educational material and researches Anne Frank's history (House website).

The Anne Frank House organisation was founded on 3 May 1957, with Otto Frank as one of its founders, to preserve the hiding place, open it to the public and draw attention to Anne's life story (annual report 2024).

What is there: the Secret Annex and Anne Frank's diaries are the main elements; the collection also holds letters, photographs, documents and objects of the Frank family, the others in hiding and their helpers, and original parts of the Annex. More than 800 items are shown online, with descriptions in Dutch (House collection page).
funding_verdict: Anne Frank House: self-funded from tickets, with lottery and project grants; no standing government subsidy
wider_context: A 2022 book by a cold-case team naming a suspect in the betrayal of the Frank family was criticised by historians and its Dutch publisher delayed a second print run; DutchNews noted that the House's own 2016 research had suggested the annex was found by accident (DutchNews, 31 January 2022). The book was not the House's.
